moduleTitle: Module 10: How to Use the App
title: 10.1 Dashboard Navigation, Header, and Layout
summary: A beginner can feel lost if a trading app looks like many different tools at once.
bodyHtml:
10.1 Dashboard Navigation, Header, and Layout

Why This Matters

A beginner can feel lost if a trading app looks like many different tools at once.

TradeQuip is easier to use when you understand one basic idea first: most day-to-day activity happens inside one main app shell. You move between tabs instead of leaving the app for a completely different product each time.

This lesson shows you the exact labels you will see on screen so you can move around without guessing.

What You Should Understand After This Lesson

By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:

  • tell the difference between the public website and the signed-in app;
  • move between the main dashboard tabs on desktop and mobile;
  • understand what the header bell, balance pill, and user menu do;
  • know how Quotes, Chart, and Account connect to each other.

Public Website Versus Signed-In App

The public website is where people read about the product.

The signed-in app is where you actually use it.

For a normal trader, the main signed-in pages are:

  • / for the main dashboard shell
  • /journal for Trading Journal
  • /profile for Profile Settings
  • /verify-email for email verification when needed

This guide focuses on the trader-facing app. It does not teach admin-only tools.

The Main Dashboard Tabs

Inside the main dashboard shell, the platform uses these exact tab labels:

Desktop Mobile What it opens
Quotes Quotes The Live Quotes screen
Chart Chart The chart screen for the selected instrument
Trade Trade The order-entry and position-management screen
History History Trade History
Leaderboard Leaders The page titled Talent
Account Account Account information and Mailbox

(Table alt-text: A six-row table showing the exact dashboard tab labels on desktop and mobile, plus what each tab opens.)

The important beginner detail is that desktop and mobile are almost the same. The one label you should notice is:

  • desktop says Leaderboard
  • mobile says Leaders

How Navigation Looks on Each Device

On Desktop

You use the left-side navigation.

On Mobile or in the Capacitor App

You use the bottom navigation bar.

The Capacitor app uses the same screens and the same wording as the web app. The main difference is layout, not product behavior.

The Header Area

At the top of the dashboard, you will see the header.

Important live labels and controls include:

  • the bell opens Notifications
  • the balance pill can show BAL: or BL:
  • stale account data can show Updating
  • the menu card can show Online
  • the menu card can show Real-time Data

From the normal trader menu, the main actions are:

  • Profile Settings
  • Sign out

This guide does not include admin-only menu actions.

Using the Notifications Panel

When you open the bell, the panel title is Notifications.

Inside it, a beginner should know these visible controls:

  • Mark all
  • the speaker icon, which toggles notification sound

You may also see messages such as:

  • Loading notifications…
  • No notifications yet.
  • Notifications are currently disabled by admin.

Using the Quotes Tab

When you open Quotes, the page title is Live Quotes.

Important controls on this screen include:

  • the search box with the placeholder Search instruments...
  • sort buttons Symbol, Price, and Change
  • status text such as Real-time Data, Market Closed, Cached Prices, Connecting..., or Offline

If quote customization is enabled for your account, the icon buttons open:

  • Add Symbols
  • Manage Symbols

Those dialogs are optional features. The main beginner skill is simpler: use Live Quotes to find an instrument and tap it.

What Happens When You Tap a Symbol

If you select a symbol while you are not already on Chart or Trade, the app moves you into Chart.

That means the app is connected on purpose:

  • Quotes helps you choose the instrument
  • Chart helps you inspect it
  • Trade helps you act on it

This is one workflow, not three unrelated pages.

Using the Chart Tab

The Chart tab opens the chart for the selected instrument.

The live chart screen currently includes:

  • period buttons 1D, 1H, 1W, and 1M
  • a floating quote box with Ask, Bid, and Spread
  • quick trade controls Sell, Lots, and Buy

If the embedded chart fails to load, you can see:

  • Chart unavailable
  • Retry

On chart-enabled screens, the quick buttons are useful for speed, but beginners should still check the symbol and price carefully before doing anything.

Using the Account Tab

The Account tab has two internal panels:

  • Account
  • Mailbox

The platform can also route directly to Mailbox from a link or notification. In URL form, that looks like:

/?tab=account&panel=mailbox

You do not need to memorize the URL. The point is that Mailbox is part of Account, not a separate dashboard tab.

Web and Capacitor App Alignment

The Capacitor app is not a different trading product.

It uses the same trader-facing screens and wording as the web app:

  • the same dashboard tabs
  • the same Trading Journal
  • the same Profile Settings
  • the same trade-screen labels

So once you learn the web app, the mobile wrapper should feel familiar.

navigate the main dashboard tabs using the exact labels users see on screen;
understand what the header controls do and what the user menu contains;
explain how symbol selection, account-panel routing, and the Capacitor wrapper affect navigation.
